questions.question_text: Heckel's plot represents ...............

options.A: Extent of plastic and elastic deformation of material during compaction

questions.explanation: Heckel's plot is used in compaction studies to relate powder porosity to the applied pressure.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would cause increase in the binding strength at the dry granulation process in significant degree
questions.explanation: Macrogol 4000 (polyethylene glycol) acts as an effective dry binder to increase mechanical strength in dry granulation.

questions.question_text: The correct statements concerning concertation microencapsulation (1) Concertation always leads to monophasic microcapsule (2) When the gelatin is used for microcapsule's wall material, the concertation is bound to happen (3) Only gelatin can be used for microcapsule's wall (4) Simple or compound concertation can be distinguished according to the number of macromolecular colloids taking part in the process (5) The pH conditions of the system and the solubility of the auxiliary materials do not have any effect on the preparation of the microcapsule
questions.explanation: Coacervation (referred to as concertation in scan typo) can be classified into simple or complex based on the number of macromolecular colloids, and gelatin is a classic wall material often associated with it.

questions.question_text: Cyclohexanone exhibits only ............... peaks in $^{13}CNMR$ spectrum due to symmetry
questions.explanation: Cyclohexanone has plane symmetry reducing its unique carbons to 4 ($C1=O$, $C2$, $C3$, $C4$, wait $C2,6$ and $C3,5$ are equivalent, giving 4 distinct signals).

questions.question_text: If an organic compound does not absorb UV visible radiation it means compound does not contain ...............
questions.explanation: UV-Vis absorption typically requires conjugated systems, chromophores, or heteroatoms with n-electrons; lack of conjugation shifts absorption out of the UV-Vis range.

questions.question_text: The positively polarized carbon atom of a carbonyl group acts as...........

options.A: An electrophile and a lewis base
options.B: A nucleophile and a lewis acid
options.C: A nucleophile and a lewis base
options.D: An electrophile and a lewis acid

questions.explanation: The carbonyl carbon is electron-deficient (positively polarized), making it an electrophile and an electron-pair acceptor (Lewis acid).

questions.question_text: The Pinene hydrochloride rearranged into bornylterpenoid is called as...........

options.B: A nucleophile and a lewis acid

questions.explanation: The conversion of pinene hydrochloride to bornyl chloride is a classic Wagner-Meerwein carbonium ion rearrangement.

questions.question_text: The mouse model for type I diabetes mellitus is...........
questions.explanation: The Non-Obese Diabetic (NOD) mouse is the standard animal model for autoimmune Type 1 diabetes.

questions.question_text: Cholesterol contributors to ............... Of the biological membrane
questions.explanation: Cholesterol buffers membrane fluidity, preventing extremes of too much fluidity or rigidity across temperatures.

questions.question_text: Active site for all serine proteases consists of which triad
questions.explanation: The catalytic triad of serine proteases classically consists of Serine, Histidine, and Aspartate.

questions.question_text: ..........., Anthelmintics having Immunosuppressant activity.
questions.explanation: Levamisole is an anthelmintic agent that also possesses immunomodulatory/immunosuppressant properties.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is selective $\alpha_2$ selective antagonist
questions.explanation: Yohimbine is a well-known competitive $\alpha_2$-adrenergic receptor antagonist.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is NOT a protoplast fusion agent
questions.explanation: Colchicine is a mitotic inhibitor (microtubule polymerization blocker), not a fusogen for protoplast fusion.

questions.question_text: Clinically used Labetolol is ...............
questions.explanation: Labetalol has two chiral centers and the clinically used active isomer combination is (1R, 1'S)-Labetalol (R, S).

questions.question_text: For intramuscular injection, angle of administration is ............... Degree
questions.explanation: Intramuscular injections are administered at a 90-degree angle to reach deep muscle tissue.

questions.question_text: Aromatase is an enzyme complex that is the target for several anticancer drugs. Which of the following anticancer drugs targets aromatase
questions.explanation: Aminoglutethimide is an aromatase inhibitor used in breast cancer treatment.

questions.question_text: Vinca alkaloids that are used in combination therapy to treat a variety of tumors. How to cancer cells normally gain resistance to these agents

options.B: Overexpression of the carrier protein called P- glycoprotein
options.D: Decreased ability of the drug to enter target cells

questions.explanation: Tumors typically develop multi-drug resistance against vinca alkaloids via overexpression of P-glycoprotein efflux pumps.

questions.question_text: A set of closely related genes of generic markers that are inherited as a single unit is
questions.explanation: A haplotype is a combination of alleles or gene markers on a single chromosome that are inherited together.

questions.question_text: Ginseng saponins belong to the series of ...............
questions.explanation: Ginsenosides (ginseng saponins) are primarily triterpene saponins of the dammarane series.

questions.question_text: Stokes Einstein equation to the series of ...............

options.A: Enegy changes in Sedimentaition suspension setting

questions.explanation: The Stokes-Einstein equation relates the diffusion coefficient of spherical particles to particle radius and solvent viscosity.

questions.question_text: The source of radiation for FAR IR spectrometer is ...............
questions.explanation: A high-pressure mercury arc lamp is commonly used as a radiation source in the far-infrared region.

questions.question_text: Which of the following alkaloids derived from lysine
questions.explanation: Lobeline is a piperidine alkaloid derived biosynthetically from lysine.

questions.question_text: The agent that can only be given intravenously for heart failure is ...............
questions.explanation: Dobutamine is a catecholamine with a very short half-life requiring continuous intravenous infusion.

questions.question_text: A prescription order for an antibiotic preparation includes the directions 'ii gtt AU q.i.d' what auxiliary label should be affixed to the prescription order container
questions.explanation: AU stands for 'aurque utraque' which means both ears, so the auxiliary label should specify 'For the ear'.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following amino acid residues is specifically recognized by chymotrypsin during peptide bond cleavage
questions.explanation: Chymotrypsin preferentially cleaves peptide bonds at the C-terminal side of large hydrophobic amino acid residues like Phenylalanine (Phe), Tryptophan, and Tyrosine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following criteria should be considered when reviewing a medication for addition to the hospital formulary

options.A: The amount of samples provided to hospital physicians
options.B: Research funds donated to the hospital by the pharmaceutical company
options.D: Whether is a gluten-free oral formulation

questions.explanation: Safety profile and national adverse drug reaction reports are critical clinical criteria when evaluating drugs for a hospital formulary.

questions.question_text: Identify the GABA reuptake inhibitor
questions.explanation: Tiagabine (often spelled Tigabine in exams) is a selective GABA reuptake inhibitor (GAT-1).

questions.question_text: What in the reason of complicated penetration of some drugs through brain-blood barrier

options.A: High lipid solubility of a drug
options.B: High endocytosis degree in a brain capillary
options.C: Absence of pores in the brain capillary endothelium

questions.explanation: The blood-brain barrier features tight junctions and the absence of fenestrations (pores) in endothelial cells, restricting paracellular drug penetration.

questions.question_text: Reynold's number is given by ...............
questions.explanation: Reynolds number (Re) is defined as inertial forces divided by viscous forces: $Re = \rho VD/\mu$.

questions.question_text: The increase in concentration of second messengers (cAMP, cGMP, Ca^{2+} etc.) leads to:

options.A: Inhibition of intracellular protein kinases and protein phosphorylation
options.B: Protein kinases activation and protein phosphorylation
options.C: blocking of interaction between a receptor and an effector

questions.explanation: Secondary messengers like cAMP activate protein kinases (e.g., PKA) leading to downstream protein phosphorylation cascades.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cholinomimetics activates both muscarinic and nicotinic receptors
questions.explanation: Carbachol possesses both potent muscarinic and nicotinic receptor agonist activity.

questions.question_text: Deoxy position of deoxyribose in DNA is at ...............
questions.explanation: Deoxyribose lacks an oxygen atom at the C-2' position compared to ribose.

questions.question_text: All are potent 3A4 inhibitors EXCEPT ...............
questions.explanation: Barbiturates are classic inducers of CYP3A4, not inhibitors.

questions.question_text: 'Probability of nonsterility' is given by ...............
questions.explanation: Sterility Assurance Level (SAL) or probability of non-sterility is typically calculated using kinetic parameters but not directly represented by F, Z, or D values alone which describe thermal destruction time.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a selective medium for the growth of vibreocholerae
questions.explanation: TCBS (Thiosulfate-citrate-bile salts-sucrose) agar is the selective and differential medium used for the isolation of Vibrio cholerae.

questions.question_text: Specific conductance unit is ...............
questions.explanation: Specific conductance (conductivity) is expressed in Siemens per cm or $Mho\ cm^{-1}$.

questions.question_text: Karplus curve is associated with which spectroscopy
questions.explanation: The Karplus equation relates ${}^3J$ coupling constants to dihedral angles in 1H NMR spectroscopy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pair of volumetric method of argentometric titration and indicator used is matched correctly (1) Fajan's Method: Chromate (2) Mohr's method: Fluroescein (3) Vohlard's method: Ferric salt. The method and indicator matches correctly in ...............
questions.explanation: Volhard's method uses ferric alum (ferric salt) as an indicator. Mohr's uses chromate, Fajan's uses fluorescein (the pairs in 1 and 2 are swapped).

questions.question_text: The reaction of the citric acid cycle that is most similar to the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex catalyzed conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA is the conversion of
questions.explanation: The alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex mechanism and coenzymes are virtually identical to the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following pairs of lipids & related compounds exhibist opposite biological activities
questions.explanation: 5-HPETE is a precursor/intermediate, whereas Leukotriene D4 is a potent bronchoconstrictor/inflammatory mediator acting downstream or via different pathways compared to general precursors.

questions.question_text: HIV may NOT respond to ...............
questions.explanation: Neuraminidase inhibitors (e.g., oseltamivir) are used for influenza virus, not HIV.

questions.question_text: Palmitic, oleic or stearic acid ester of cholesterol used manufacture of cosmetic creams is ...............
questions.explanation: Lanolin consists predominantly of sterol esters (cholesterol esters) of fatty acids like palmitic, oleic, and stearic acids.

questions.question_text: ..........., Is needed for suspensions, lotions, emulsions, creams and ointments to keeps a high container consistency and yet pour and spread easily when needed. It also is satisfactory for IM slow release yet easy to inject
questions.explanation: Thixotropy is the property where gels or fluids thin out upon shearing (shaking/pouring) and recover at rest, ideal for suspensions and creams.

questions.question_text: The enzyme superoxide dismutase (SOD) converts
questions.explanation: Superoxide dismutase catalyzes the dismutation of superoxide radicals into molecular oxygen and hydrogen peroxide.

questions.question_text: For first order reactions the rate constant, k, has the units as ...............
questions.explanation: First-order reaction rate constants have units of inverse time ($s^{-1}$ or $time^{-1}$).

questions.question_text: Which of the following may be used to assess the relative bioavailability of two chemically equivalent drug product in a crossover study

options.D: Area under the plasma level time curve

questions.explanation: Area Under the Curve (AUC) is the primary pharmacokinetic parameter used to assess relative bioavailability.

questions.question_text: A 25.0 mL sample of a solution of a monoprotic acid is titrated with a $0.115\ M\ NaOH$ solution the titration curve shows equivalence point at 7.05. which of the following indicators would be best for this titration
questions.explanation: An equivalence point near 7.05 represents a neutral titration endpoint best matched by bromothymol blue (pH range ~6.0-7.6).

questions.question_text: Which of the following in termed as mass filter
questions.explanation: A quadrupole mass spectrometer acts as a mass filter by allowing only ions of a specific m/z to pass through.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is produced in phenyl propanoid pathway
questions.explanation: The phenylpropanoid pathway produces various phenolic compounds, flavonoids, and lignin starting from phenylalanine.

questions.question_text: A diode array detector coupled with UV detection is advantageous because it

options.B: Allow lower concentrations of analyte to be detected
options.C: Speeds up the detection at a single wavelength
options.D: Allows a single wavelength of detection to be moreprecisely chosen

questions.explanation: Diode array detectors (DAD) capture a wide spectrum of wavelengths simultaneously.

questions.question_text: The LOD of an analysis is at the femtogram level. This corresponds to detection at the
questions.explanation: Femtogram ($10^{-15}$ g) detection level corresponds to parts-per-quadrillion or $10^{-15}$ scale.

questions.question_text: Which are those therapeutic systems, which liberate the active ingredient through a special hole, prepared by laser
questions.explanation: OROS (Oral Osmotic) systems utilize laser-drilled delivery orifices to release drug osmotically.

questions.question_text: Which of following chromatographic technique is most suitable for small, nonvolatile water-insoluble solutes
questions.explanation: Reverse-phase liquid chromatography is standard for small, non-volatile, water-insoluble or hydrophobic molecules.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antiviral agent in not a nucleoside analog
questions.explanation: Moroxydine is a biguanide derivative antiviral, not a nucleoside analog.

questions.question_text: Regarding two compartment pharmcokenitics all are true EXCEPT

options.A: A drug is always removed from the peripheral compartment
options.B: A drug with a high volume of distribution is likely to be lipophilic
options.C: A drug can have a short duration of action while being eliminated very slowly
options.D: Most anesthetic drugs are modelled well with a two-compartment model

questions.explanation: Drugs are eliminated from the central compartment, not the peripheral compartment.

questions.question_text: Phenothiazine is obtained by ............... with sulfur
questions.explanation: Phenothiazine is synthesized by the reaction of diphenylamine with sulfur in the presence of a catalyst.

questions.question_text: Vitamin K is constituted of ............... ring
questions.explanation: Vitamin K derivatives contain a 2-methyl-1,4-naphthoquinone ring structure.

questions.question_text: To balace intellectual property protection, competition and access to affordable prescription drug, the act made by US government is
questions.explanation: The Drug Price Competition and Patent Term Restoration Act of 1984 is widely known as the Hatch-Waxman Act.

questions.question_text: Gridnard test is used for the detection of ...............

questions.question_text: Which hormone works antagonistically to parathormone ...............
questions.explanation: Calcitonin (spelled Cakitronin in scan typo) lowers blood calcium levels, acting antagonistically to parathyroid hormone (parathormone).

questions.question_text: Drugs that have been found to be useful in one or more types of heart failure include all of the following EXCEPT ...............
questions.explanation: Alpha-adrenoreceptor agonists cause vasoconstriction and increase afterload, worsening heart failure.

questions.explanation: The Ames test uses histidine-auxotrophic strains of Salmonella typhimurium to assess mutagenicity.

questions.explanation: Thiamine pyrophosphate is involved in pyruvate decarboxylation (iii-c), tetrahydrofolate in nucleotide methylation like uridine to thymidine (ii-a), and transamination/dehydrogenation pathways involve other cofactors.

questions.question_text: Drugs that show nonlinear pharmacokinetics have which of the following property

options.A: A constant ratio of drug metabolites is formed as the administered dose increase.
options.B: The elimination half - life increasing as the administered dose increase
options.C: The area under the plasma drug concentration versus time curve increasing in direct proportion to an increase in the administered dose.
options.D: Both low and high doses follow first order elimination kinetics

questions.explanation: In saturable (nonlinear) pharmacokinetics, half-life changes and typically increases as the dose increases due to enzyme saturation.

questions.question_text: Appropriate reasons for the deviation form the beer's law among the following are (P) Mnsonchromaticity of light (Q) Very high concentration of analyte (R) Association of analyte (S) Dissociation of analyte
